newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, China to boost economic, trade ties.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, China to boost economic, trade ties.

text.p: Visiting Chinese Vice Premier Li Lanqing is holding talks in Bulgaria on ways to revive economic ties neglected since the end of Communist rule in the Balkan state, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister said on Monday.

"We are discussing concrete ways to boost trade and cooperation between the two countries and to seek joint presence in third (countries') markets, including investment," Doncho Konakchiev said after talks with the Chinese delegation.
Bulgaria's biggest fertiliser producer Himko on Monday signed a contract with China's Xinohem to supply 150,000 tonnes of urea per year.
"Our contract is for a year but there is a clause for prolonging it," Himko's executive director Kiril Petkov told Reuters.

Officials speaking on the second day of Li's four-day visit said Bulgaria and China planned to set up joint ventures to produce bicycles, pharmaceutical products, shoes, televisions, small tractors, and other light industrial products.
They said Chinese firms were interested in importing Bulgarian equipment for the production of fruit juice. Bulgaria's trade interests included coal supplies from China.
"There are also perspectives for cooperation in the fields of banking, insurance and high technology," Konakchiev told reporters.
He said there was scope for bringing current annual trade of less than $50 million back up to its 1990 levels.
The Chinese delegation presented Bulgaria with a 2,000-line digital telephone exchange worth $400,000, Bulgarian deputy trade minister Serafim Sofroniev said.
"This is the beginning of our cooperation as the Chinese exchange matches with our exchanges, supplied by (France's) Alcatel and Siemens AG," Sofroniev said.
